title: Does Faith Build Stronger Families?: UVA’s Brad Wilcox Shares the Data | Institute for Family Studies
gist: An IFS news listing of a Fox News Lighthouse Faith podcast episode in which UVA's Brad Wilcox argues children from stable two-parent homes do better in school and regular worship attendance strengthens marriages, urging that family structure be factored into explanations of school performance gaps.

insights.claim: Brad Wilcox argues children from stable two-parent homes excel in school, and that explanations of performance disparities should factor in family structure and marriage data rather than only economic gaps or systemic issues.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Pushes education-policy debate toward family structure as a driver of achievement gaps, a contested alternative to resource-based explanations.
insights.quote: While schools often blame economic gaps or systemic issues for performance disparities, Brad argues it’s time to factor family structure and marriage data into the equation.
insights.locator: University of Virginia Research Professor and Author

insights.claim: Wilcox's research holds that parents who attend worship services regularly have stronger marriages.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Links declining religious attendance to weaker family stability.
insights.quote: parents who attend worship services regularly have stronger marriages
insights.locator: University of Virginia Research Professor and Author

insights.claim: Wilcox's book 'Get Married' argues Americans should defy elites and forge strong families to save civilization, framing family formation as a civilizational issue.
insights.speaker: Institute for Family Studies
insights.so_what: Signals an advocacy push for pro-marriage policy and cultural messaging.
insights.locator: University of Virginia Research Professor and Author
